note:
Measured 2026-07-28 from the first working reference and implementation across all eighteen Golden cases, then reviewed and committed. Regenerating these from a later run would defeat their purpose: a tolerance is an input to validation, not an output of it.

The oracle runs bfloat16 on CUDA and the port runs F32 on CPU, so these thresholds cover a dtype and a device difference as well as an implementation one.

This file briefly claimed that was "the comparison the contract asks for" while the contract's dtype section forbade it. The contract was revised on 2026-07-30: the prohibition was a rule no BF16-checkpoint family could follow, because the same document pins the oracle to the checkpoint's dtype and the replay to CPU, and ggml computes a stored BF16 weight through F32. An unequal-arithmetic comparison is now permitted on three conditions, and this stage meets all three: it is named in reference_stage above, the deep talker probes gate on cosine rather than max-abs, and structural exactness comes from the replayed codes rather than from any threshold here.

The condition the revision imposes and this file does not yet satisfy: **the dtype and implementation components of each threshold are not separated.** They are measurable without the port -- the talker probes are captured on the prefill, which draws nothing, so the same oracle at two dtypes can be compared directly -- and that measurement has not been run. Until it is, every figure below is a combined one, and a regression could hide inside the dtype allowance.

Talker probes gate on cosine similarity, not max-abs. The deep layers carry outlier channels ahead of the final norm: max-abs reaches 17.4 at L27 while cosine holds at 0.99992, and a max-abs threshold would report catastrophic failure on a correct port. This was predicted from the reference port before any measurement existed and the measurements have the same shape. Max-abs is recorded per probe as observed, for review rather than for gating.

The waveform gates on both. A listener hears the waveform, and a cosine over it would hide a constant offset.

Every threshold is five times the measured deviation in (1 - cosine). That headroom is wide enough to absorb run-to-run variation and far tighter than any defect this suite has caught: a transposed code stream gave cosine 0.017, and a prompt built one position short gave -0.01.

The grid is keyed on Quantization Profile, Execution Backend and stage, which is what tests/python/test_tolerance_coverage.py checks. BF16 is recorded on CPU only: the source profile was never swept on CUDA, and listing a cell that was not measured is the hole that test exists to close.

BF16 was swept on CUDA on 2026-07-29; the note above about it being CPU-only is superseded by the cell itself.

A retracted claim, kept because the reasoning error is the useful part. This file previously recorded that requesting SYNTH_BACKEND_CUDA at the public seam moved the sampled path onto the accelerator, on the evidence that the dialect case drew ten frames on CUDA against eleven on CPU. That comparison used two different binaries -- a Release CPU build against the CUDA preset -- and optimization level alone changes CPU float contraction enough to move a draw. Re-run with one binary across five cases in three languages and three Voices, CPU and CUDA return identical frame counts every time; only the waveform differs, which is the codec's arithmetic. The placement is what stage 7 measured: the codec moves, the sampled path does not.

case_count corrected to 20 on 2026-07-31 when the manifest cross-check landed; the per-stage 'cases' fields record each sweep's size at measurement time and are deliberately unchanged.

Restructured to per-variant `case_count` on 2026-08-11's review round: this file used to carry a flat top-level `case_count: 20` (the historical sentence directly above this one, from 2026-07-31, describes what that number meant while it was the only one -- it is not retracted, only superseded). That flat key was correct for qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-customvoice alone but silently meaningless once qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base's manifest (12 cases) started pointing at this same file: tests/python/test_golden_manifests.py's test_tolerance_case_count_matches_manifest read exactly one top-level key, so a second variant sharing this file did not fail that check, it disabled it for the whole family. tests/tolerances/vits.json already carries two variants this same way (`variants.<name>.case_count`), which this file now follows: `variants.qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-customvoice.case_count` is the same 20 the historical sentence above describes, moved rather than changed; `variants.qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base.case_count` is 12, tracking that manifest's own case count, not a measurement -- see `variants.qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base`'s own note for what is and is not actually measured there.

test_tolerance_case_count_matches_manifest was extended in the same commit to check `variants.<name>.case_count` when a file uses this shape, rather than only the flat key -- which also means it now actually runs for VITS's two variants for the first time; it silently skipped both before, for the identical reason it silently skipped qwen3-tts.

A second review round on 2026-08-11 found this file's first restructuring had broken scripts/validate-qwen3-tts-replay.py, which reads this grid by profile/backend/stage with no variant coordinate: moving `profiles` under `variants.<name>` left it unable to resolve any cell, including for the published customvoice variant. Fixed in the validator, not by moving `profiles` back -- it already loads the manifest and therefore already knows `manifest["variant"]`, the coordinate it was missing. That round also found that qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base's checked stage set (`variants.qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base.profiles`) had briefly included `speaker_encoder`/`codec_encoder` alongside `public`/`replay`, which made tests/python/test_tolerance_coverage.py's validator-coverage check pass for a stage with no validator and no measurement behind it -- proved by constructing exactly that state for a `vocoder_polish` stage on the published customvoice grid and watching the relaxed check let it through. `speaker_encoder`/`codec_encoder` moved out to `provisional_variants.qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base`, a sibling key `measured_variants()` does not read, and the validator-coverage check was exact equality again. **Both halves of that sentence stopped being true on 2026-08-14 and it is corrected here rather than left to contradict the variant note two hundred lines below.** `provisional_variants` is GONE -- `codec_encoder` was its last occupant and now sits in the Base BF16 grid as a real measured stage. And the coverage check is no longer exact equality: it requires every validator to have a measurement in at least ONE variant and every measured stage to have a validator, because exact per-variant equality became unsatisfiable once a capability existed in one variant and not another (this variant has a codec encoder; customvoice's package does not contain one).

The branch's final review, 2026-08-12: the top-level `suite_version` and `status` were the last two fields left describing one variant while the file described two. `status: thresholds-committed-and-enforced` and `suite_version: 2` were both true of qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-customvoice and both false of qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base, whose grid holds placeholders and whose manifest is at suite_version 1. Both now sit per-variant beside `case_count`, following the same restructuring as that key. The top-level `suite_version` is kept at 2 and the top-level `status` now points at the per-variant fields rather than asserting one of them: tests/python/test_tolerance_coverage.py requires a top-level `status` to exist, and a file-wide claim about a file describing two variants at different maturities cannot be true.

replay.description: The oracle's codes replayed through the port on CPU, compared against its prefill probes and waveform.
replay.note:
Extended to twenty cases on 2026-07-29 with two utterances roughly twice the previous longest -- 18.7 and 21.3 seconds against 9.3. Every committed threshold held and not one worst-case figure moved: the new cases are better than the suite worst on every probe (talker.final 0.999776 and 0.999677 against the suite's 0.999452).

So this port does not degrade with length, which is worth stating because the truncation defect found by ear did appear only past the old maximum. That was the sampler, not accumulation, and these cases exist so the suite reaches the lengths where a defect of that shape lives.

public.note: Behavioural rather than numeric. This stage has no probes: it gates on relations between runs -- that one seed reproduces and another does not, that a Voice change moves the audio -- which hold within a backend and cannot be expressed as a threshold against the oracle.

replay.description: The source profile with the codec on CUDA and the autoregressive half on CPU.
replay.note:
The gap this closes: the accelerator work was done under F16, so the source profile had never been swept on CUDA and the grid claimed CPU only.

Every talker probe is bit-for-bit equal to this profile's CPU entry, which is the placement proving itself -- the talker feeds a sampled code and stays on the CPU, so only the waveform can move, and it does: 0.999427 to 0.999404.

Against F16 on CUDA the waveform is identical to six digits, 0.999404 at a max-abs of 0.1602 under both. The codec is almost entirely F32 in either package, so the profile has little left to change there. That is read off the tensor types, not a tested cause.

Eighteen cases: the two longer ones were added the same day and their oracle artifacts postdate this sweep.

public.description: The public C seam driven end to end under the source profile on CUDA.
public.note: Behavioural rather than numeric; see the BF16 CPU entry.

replay.description: The F16 profile replayed on CPU against the same oracle artifacts as the source profile.
replay.note:
F16 halves the talker half and leaves the codec at the reference dtype, so its waveform agreement is identical to the source profile's -- the codec that produced it is the same F32 graph. The talker probes are marginally tighter than the source's because F16 carries ten mantissa bits against bfloat16's seven.

This profile is the same size as the source, 2168 MB. What it buys is time: ggml's CPU bfloat16 matrix multiply is far slower than its F16 one, and halving weights that were already two bytes wide took a 37-frame case from 43.0 seconds to 9.6.

public.note: Behavioural rather than numeric. This stage has no probes: it gates on relations between runs -- that one seed reproduces and another does not, that a Voice change moves the audio -- which hold within a backend and cannot be expressed as a threshold against the oracle.

replay.description: The F16 profile with the codec on CUDA and the autoregressive half on CPU, against the same oracle artifacts.
replay.note:
Placement is proven by the measurements rather than asserted: every talker probe is identical to the CPU stage's, because the talker did not move and could not -- its output feeds a sampled code, which docs/backends.md holds on the CPU. Only the waveform changed, and only in the sixth decimal of its cosine, which is the codec's tensor-core arithmetic.

The stage exists because the codec is 41 percent of wall clock under this profile and 35 times faster there: 8.44 seconds to 0.24 on a 37-frame case, taking the whole synthesis from 20.69 to 12.50.

replay.description: The Q8_MIXED profile replayed on CPU against the same oracle artifacts.
replay.note:
Only the autoregressive half is quantized. The codec stays F32, so the waveform agreement is identical to the other profiles' to six digits -- the graph that produced it did not change. What moved is the talker: its final hidden state and logits drop from a cosine of 0.9994 to 0.9956, about eight times the deviation.

That matters more than the unchanged waveform suggests. Replay supplies the codes, so this stage cannot show what a logits difference of that size does to a draw. In normal operation it will select different codes sometimes, exactly as a different backend does. The package is 1359 MiB against 2169, and synthesis of a 9.6 second case ran at a real-time factor of 0.85 against F16's 1.24.

qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base.note:
case_count (12) tracks this variant's manifest (tests/golden/qwen3-tts/qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base.manifest.json), not a measurement.

`public` is still an honest empty placeholder (see its own `description`): `checks: 0` / `all_passed: null`, because no public-seam run exists yet for this variant.

`replay` carries exactly one real probe, `speaker.x_vector`, over the two cases (base-xvector-en, base-xvector-zh) whose oracle dump and C++ port both exist -- see that probe's own `note`. The deep talker/audio probes customvoice's `replay` carries (`talker.hidden_l*`, `talker.final`, `talker.logits`, `audio.pcm`) are still unmeasured here: this variant has no autoregressive replay in the grid yet, so `replay.cases` stays at 2 and this status stays partial.

`codec_encoder` became a real measured stage on 2026-08-14. It replaces `provisional_variants.qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base`, a sibling container this file carried until that date, whose `codec_encoder` held eight probes copied verbatim from customvoice's BF16 `replay` stage -- a different model's talker prefill probes, not this stage's own tensors, as that entry's own description said plainly. `speaker_encoder` had lived beside it under the identical caveat with the identical copied numbers, and was retired on 2026-08-12 the day a real speaker cell existed. `codec_encoder` is retired the same way and for the same reason: keeping both would describe one subsystem twice, once as an honest placeholder and once as an actual measurement, and the placeholder is the one with nothing left to say. The container is gone entirely, because that entry was its last occupant.

The stage/validator relation changed shape on 2026-08-14, and the sentence that used to stand here was wrong for six tasks -- it claimed this variant's checked stage set equals the family-wide validator set {public, replay}, which stopped being true the moment scripts/validate-qwen3-tts-codec_encoder.py was committed and left tests/python/test_tolerance_coverage.py red for BOTH variants, unnoticed because that test was not registered with CTest. It is registered now (synthesize-tolerance-coverage). The rule it enforces is no longer per-variant exact equality: every validator must have a measurement in at least ONE variant, and every measured stage must have a validator. This variant measures {codec_encoder, public, replay}; qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-customvoice measures {public, replay} and correctly does not carry codec_encoder, because its package does not contain a codec encoder at all -- 657 tensors against this variant's 894, the 237-tensor difference being exactly 76 speaker_encoder + 161 codec encoder (see the family record's tensor census and its 'The codec encoder is not carried' section). Under the old rule, measuring the codec encoder on the variant that HAS one would have forced five fabricated codec_encoder cells into customvoice's BF16/F16/Q8_MIXED grids and their CUDA sub-grids.

public.description: PROVISIONAL placeholder, not yet measured. No public-seam check has ever been run against qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base: no C++ port or converter output exists yet for it (Tasks 4 through 10 build that). This key exists only so this variant's stage set satisfies tests/python/test_tolerance_coverage.py's family-wide validator check (scripts/validate-qwen3-tts-public.py exists and is family-wide, not per-variant) ahead of any real run against this variant. `checks: 0` and `all_passed: null` are deliberately not customvoice's `8`/`true` -- copying those would claim a result that has never happened.

replay.description: The Base variant's deterministic conditioning half on CPU: reference audio through the mel front end and the ECAPA-TDNN speaker encoder, compared against the oracle's own x-vector. The autoregressive half is not yet replayed here -- only the two x-vector-only cases can be driven end to end until Plan 3 lands ICL.

prompt.icl_embed.normalizer: relative deviation = ||port - oracle|| / ||oracle||, per compared tensor. NOT a cosine, so this file's `1 - 5*(1 - observed)` cosine rule does not apply to it; the analogous widening would be 5x the measured deviation.
prompt.icl_embed.note:
The two-track ICL prompt: text track, codec track, their summed block, the block as it sits in the assembled prefill, and the trailing schedule -- five comparisons against the oracle's own dump, all gated at the same bound. Enforced by tests/qwen3_tts_icl_prompt_real.cpp, which since 2026-08-14 READS this number rather than carrying its own copy of it.

REQUIRED BY THE PLAN AND MISSING UNTIL NOW. Step 4 lists `prompt.icl_embed` as a committed probe; it existed only as five hardcoded `2.0e-2` literals in C++, so the one deliverable of this task -- the tolerance contract -- had a hole in it that no test could see.

THE GATE IS DELIBERATELY TIGHTER THAN THIS FILE'S WIDENING RULE WOULD MAKE IT, and that is why it was not recomputed. 2.0e-2 is the value already enforced; the measured worst is 8.734e-03, so it carries 2.29x headroom. Applying a 5x widening to the measurement would give 4.37e-02 and LOOSEN a gate that is currently passing -- an enforced bound is never relaxed to match a formula. The 2.0e-2 also has its own justification, which the C++ comment records: bfloat16's unit roundoff is 2**-8 = 3.906e-03, so this is about five bf16 roundings, and the port's float32 arithmetic over the package's bf16 tables accumulates on top of one rounding.

It is not wide enough for a shifted track to hide in: a one-position shift moves these deviations by O(1) relative, which Task 7's rule-deletion round measured directly. Note that `block` and `prefill_tail` are identical in all three cases -- expected, since the block is concatenated unchanged at the end of the prefill, and the pair is what shows that placement did not perturb it.

replay.note:
Measured 2026-08-12 on CPU (build/, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release) over base-xvector-en and base-xvector-zh, via scripts/validate-qwen3-tts-replay.py --compare-x-vector against the real qwen3-tts-12hz-0-6b-base-BF16.gguf and models/qwen3-tts-reference-audio/clone.wav. The gate is 5x the measured deviation in (1 - cosine), the rule this file's own top-level note states for every other probe here. max_abs is recorded but does not gate: an x-vector is a direction consumed by a dot product against the prompt, so cosine is the quantity that matters, the same reasoning that leaves max_abs ungated on the talker probes above and gating only on audio.pcm.

Only one independent measurement, not two: both cases point at the identical reference clip with no trim, and every file under speaker/ is byte-identical between them (conventions.json's own measurement_coverage note) -- only the synthesis text and language differ, which the speaker path never reads. Running both is what shows the whole pipeline (load, resample, encode, mel, ECAPA, x-vector) is deterministic case to case, not a second data point on the residual.

The residual is bfloat16 quantization of the *oracle*, not a port defect. The oracle's own speaker_encoder weights run in torch.bfloat16 and its dumped tensors round-trip through bfloat16 exactly for seven of the eight speaker/*.f32 files -- verified directly, max abs diff 0.0 -- everything except mel.f32, whose bf16 round-trip differs by up to ~0.031 (conventions.json's own artifact_dtypes note). At the x-vector's own largest element (|ref| = 7.28), 0.02111 is 0.68 of one bfloat16 ulp; recomputing the oracle's own final ASP/FC layer directly in float64 disagrees with the oracle's recorded x_vector by more (0.022367) than this port does. A tolerance whose story was 'the filterbank rounds differently' would be wrong: the mel front end that feeds this graph is essentially exact on its own (max_abs 3.31e-4 against the oracle, and against a float64 truth the port's own mel is *closer* -- 1.14e-4 against the oracle's 2.21e-4). The budget spent here is almost entirely the ECAPA graph's bf16-quantized-weights arithmetic across 38 convolutions, not the mel stage -- the mel comparison above was run specifically to rule the mel stage out before this number was committed, not merely alongside it.

cases_not_extended.note:
Task 12 was asked to extend this stage past its two cases and MEASURED THAT DOING SO WOULD ADD NOTHING, so it stayed at two. All ten ICL cases now have oracle dumps, and their speaker/x_vector.f32 files are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the two x-vector cases already here -- one sha256 across ten of the twelve cases. That is expected rather than surprising: every one of them points at the same untrimmed clone.wav, and the speaker path reads nothing else (not the text, not the language, not the seed). Raising `cases` from 2 to 10 on that evidence would multiply the same measurement by five and call it coverage.

THE ONLY TWO CASES THAT WOULD ADD A DATA POINT are base-ref-min and base-ref-max, whose x-vectors do differ (three distinct digests across the twelve) because their reference audio is trimmed to 1 s and looped to 30 s respectively. They are also the two this comparison cannot currently drive: run_compare_x_vector hands the driver the WAV path and the driver has no trim, so the port would encode the full clip while the oracle encoded a trimmed one, and the comparison would fail for a reason that is not the port's arithmetic. Giving the driver `trim_seconds` is what would make this stage genuinely wider, and it is not done here; the x-vector residual therefore still rests on ONE reference clip, exactly as this stage's own probe note already says.

codec_encoder.description: The Base variant's reference-audio codec encoder, compared stage by stage: waveform through the eleven-convolution SEANet stack, the frame downsampler, the eight-layer transformer and the sixteen-stage split RVQ. Three artifact sets in the same on-disk element order -- this port (F32), an upstream float32 re-run (scripts/dump_reference_qwen3_tts_codec_encoder_float32.py) and the committed bfloat16 oracle dump -- so port vs upstream-f32 isolates this port's own arithmetic while port vs oracle carries the oracle's bf16 rounding. Gated by scripts/validate-qwen3-tts-codec_encoder.py.

codec.chain.note:
THE PRIMARY GATE, and the only one of the three independent of the codebook table being shared by construction. One threshold enforced PER STAGE across all 33 taps (waveform, seanet_stage0-3, seanet_tail, transformer_l0-7, downsample, latents, rvq_residual_s00-15, rvq_reconstruction) by scripts/validate-qwen3-tts-codec_encoder.py, which prints every stage's own figure -- so a drifting stage is LOCATED in the validator's output, and this cell records the gate plus the worst stage that cleared it. Rolling the taps into one summary number is what the eleven-plus taps exist to avoid; one threshold applied to each of them is not that, it is how the validator is written.

`rel_absmax` is max|a-b| divided by the REFERENCE tensor's own absolute maximum -- one scalar scale for the whole tensor, not a per-element |d|/|x|. Quoting it against a `rel_rms` threshold is a review round the validator's own header exists to avoid repeating.

The comparison gated here is port vs upstream-f32, BOTH float32, where a defect in this port would live. Port vs the bfloat16 oracle is a different quantity that is expected to sit at bf16 scale and is not gated by this number. 1.0e-3 is still a quarter of one bf16 unit (2^-8), so it cannot be passed by a port that merely rounds like bf16 -- it demands float32 agreement with upstream. The injected fault is upstream's own symmetric (non-causal) MimiConv1d padding split, which builds the same shapes from the same weights and a different encoder: it reads 1.649, a 1650x discrimination.
codec.chain.normalizer: rel_absmax = max|a-b| / max|reference|, one scalar scale for the whole tensor -- NOT a per-element |d|/|x|, and not rel_rms. The gated comparison is port vs upstream-f32 (both float32); the second column, `observed_upstream_f32_vs_oracle_rel_absmax`, is upstream-f32 against the oracle -- it isolates the oracle's own bf16 rounding and does not involve this port at all.
codec.chain.per_stage_note:
Every tap the validator compares, worst over the three cases, measured 2026-08-14 -- the figures this grid previously did not carry. One threshold (rel_absmax above) is enforced against each of them; these are the observations it clears, not 33 separate gates.

WHERE THE PORT IS TIGHT, which the next plan will want. Thirteen of the 33 taps sit below 0.003 of one bf16 unit, and the eight transformer layers l0-l6 hold ~8e-07 (0.0002 bf16 units) -- four orders of magnitude under the gate. Two taps are EXACTLY zero: `waveform` (the port is handed the oracle's own waveform, so this is an input check, not a result) and `rvq_reconstruction` (see the stage note -- a consistency check whose operands are shared by construction).

WHERE IT IS LOOSEST, and it is a cascade rather than a defect: transformer_l7 at 9.303e-05 (0.0238 bf16 units) is the worst single tap, and the RVQ residuals climb monotonically s00 -> s15 (1.3e-05 -> 7.8e-05) because each stage subtracts the previous one's reconstruction and inherits its error. Every one of them remains an order of magnitude under the gate.

A KEY WAS RENAMED ON 2026-08-14 AND NO VALUE MOVED. These second figures were committed as `observed_port_vs_oracle_rel_absmax`; they are what scripts/validate-qwen3-tts-codec_encoder.py:206 computes, which is deviation(upstream_f32, oracle) -- printed under its own `upstream-f32 vs oracle` column header -- so they are now named that. The two quantities are numerically close (transformer_l7 is 0.4054 upstream-f32-vs-oracle against 0.4055 port-vs-oracle, a 4th-significant-digit difference) which is exactly why the mislabel survived review once. In a file that spends paragraphs naming which two things were compared, and immediately after correcting a different figure that was wrong for the same reason, the name has to be the measurement.

codec.rvq_reconstruction.semantic.note:
A PERCENTILE, NEVER A MAXIMUM, and that is measured rather than predicted. One flipped code displaces the reconstruction by about a full codebook-row separation (median |dRecon|/||e_i-e_j|| = 1.21), so this branch's per-frame maximum is 235.8 absolute against a median of 0.55, with 4 of 101 frames flipping. No bf16-scale maximum survives that, and widening one until it fit would destroy the gate. The statistic is the 95th percentile of the per-frame L2 deviation, relative to the reference frame's own L2 norm.

2.0e-2 is 5x one bf16 unit, where the design says this branch's median belongs; it flips on only 4 of 101 frames so the tail stays contained. Injected fault p95 1.601, a 78x discrimination.

The two branches get separate keys and are NEVER averaged: they are an order of magnitude apart in rms (13.5 against 3.11) and, more to the point, differ sharply in dynamic range -- this branch moves 0.004 -> 1.20 under the fault (300x) while the acoustic branch moves only 0.25 -> 1.15 (4.6x). Averaging would blunt the sharper instrument with the duller one.

codec.rvq_reconstruction.acoustic.note:
Same percentile statistic and same never-averaged rule as the semantic branch; see its note for why a maximum is unsatisfiable here.

NOT at bf16 scale, and it cannot be. This branch aggregates fifteen stages and disagreement with the bf16 oracle grows monotonically down the cascade (4, 6, 20, 34, ... 74 of 101 frames), so almost every frame carries at least one flip and the branch sits in the flip tail at the MEDIAN (0.1317), not only at its p95. The design's predicted 0.18 absolute L2 for this branch is 39x too small against a measured median of 7.014 absolute and must not be used.

HEADROOM IS ~2x HERE AND IT IS DRAWN FROM ONE RECORDING. base-ref-min is a byte-exact prefix of base-icl-en and base-text-short is that same clip again at full length: three cases, one speaker, one microphone. A second speaker would be independent corroboration and there is not one, so this figure and the semantic one should be revisited the first time a second reference clip exists, rather than treated as settled by three passing cases. Injected fault p95 1.741, a 3.5x discrimination -- the narrowest of the three gates.

codec_encoder.note:
Measured by Task 5 of the ICL plan and committed with the validator that reproduces it; promoted out of `provisional_variants` into this grid on 2026-08-14, which is what retired the copied placeholder described in this variant's own note. The thresholds and every observed figure below are transcribed from scripts/validate-qwen3-tts-codec_encoder.py, which states each one beside the measurement it clears and the injected fault it still catches; they are not re-derived here.

THE CODES ARE NOT THE GATE. The design's fourth erratum (2026-08-13) dropped plain equality on codes/reference.i32: the oracle's RVQ codebook is bfloat16 and the converter's is float32, upstream disagrees with ITSELF depending on whether `dtype` is passed at load, so an equality gate would test a load-time keyword argument rather than this port. The measured agreement rates live in `code_agreement` beside these probes, where the earlier 4.04%-versus-observed confusion is also corrected; they are observations and gate nothing. For the same reason this stage records no `codec.reference_codes` probe and the manifest carries no `alternate_grids`: enumerating admissible grids would mean committing a second oracle's output for every case.

What the reconstruction's exact zero does and does not say: port vs upstream-f32 on rvq_reconstruction measures 0 exactly, and under an injected fault it reads 1.115, so it is a comparison that CAN fail. But it decomposes into three conjuncts at once -- the codes agree, the two float32 codebook tables are bit-identical BY CONSTRUCTION, and the accumulation order matches -- so it is a consistency check, not independent evidence about the codebook conversion. The load-bearing independent evidence is `codec.chain`.

Three cases (base-icl-en, base-ref-min, base-text-short), CPU, float32 port against the committed bfloat16 oracle dump and an upstream float32 re-run of the same taps. They are one recording at three lengths, not three independent recordings -- see the acoustic probe's note.

code_agreement.note:
RECORDED AS EVIDENCE; NOTHING GATES ON IT. A correction is folded in here, because this file briefly stated the wrong thing: it read '4.04% of frame-stage decisions disagree (95.96% agreement)', conflating two different quantities. The erratum's 4.04% bounds the CODEBOOK TABLE's own contribution -- what differs when the same latent is quantized against a bf16 table versus an f32 one -- and is a FLOOR on divergence, not the observed rate. Measured end to end, port and oracle agree on 52.970% of frame-stage decisions for base-icl-en (760 of 1616 differ) and 53.846% for base-ref-min (96 of 208). Divergence grows monotonically across the 16 RVQ columns (4, 6, 20, 34 ... 74 of 101 frames for base-icl-en), which is the cascade the acoustic reconstruction gate is built around.

THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR THIS PORT is the other one: port versus upstream-f32 agrees on 100.000% of decisions, 0 of 1616, on every case. The port reproduces float32 upstream exactly; the ~47% divergence is entirely the oracle's bf16 codebook, which is why codes were removed as a gate in the first place.

gate_scope_warning.result: semantic branch FAILS the committed gate: p95 relative 0.3478 against 2.0e-2
gate_scope_warning.note:
NOTHING BELOW WAS WIDENED, AND base-ref-max WAS NOT ADDED TO `cases`. This records a gate that does not hold on a case outside the three it was calibrated on, because the rule this suite follows is that a deviation above scale gets FOUND, not accommodated.

IT IS NOT A PORT DEFECT, and three independent readings say so. On base-ref-max the port agrees with upstream-f32 on 100.000% of code decisions (0 of 6000); the continuous chain gate PASSES at 8.431e-05, tighter than base-icl-en's 9.303e-05; and the acoustic branch passes at 0.2946. The only failing quantity is the semantic reconstruction against the bfloat16 ORACLE -- a comparison in which this port does not appear on the deviating side.

THE GATE SITS ON A CLIFF AT A 5% SEMANTIC FLIP RATE, and that is the actual finding. The statistic is the 95th percentile of per-frame deviation, so it only enters the flipped-frame tail once more than 5% of frames carry a semantic flip. The three calibration cases sit at 0.00%, 3.96% and 3.96% -- all below the line, so their p95 measures unflipped frames and lands at 0.004. base-ref-max sits at 5.33%, the p95 lands inside the tail, and the figure jumps 87x to 0.3478. The gate did not drift; the percentile crossed a discontinuity.

So `2.0e-2` is not a bound on this port's semantic reconstruction in general -- it is a bound conditional on the reference's semantic flip rate staying under ~5%, which in practice means short references. That condition is undocumented in the gate itself and is exactly the kind of hidden precondition a later plan would trip over. Widening the gate to ~0.35 would make it pass here and destroy its power everywhere else: the injected fault it is meant to catch reads 1.601, only 4.6x above 0.35 rather than 78x above 0.02.

WHAT THE NEXT PLAN MUST DECIDE, and this task deliberately does not: either scope this probe by reference length (and say so in the gate), or replace the percentile with a statistic that does not have a cliff in it (a flip-rate-conditioned measure, or the median, which sits at 0.0027 here and is stable across all four cases). Until then the codec_encoder stage covers references up to 101 frames, which is what `cases: 3` and `case_ids` describe.
